mainTopic: Proof and payment for improvements when a creditor collects land, and the laws of paying hired workers on time
overview: The amud opens with land that a בעל חוב is collecting from יתומים, where each side claims it made the improvement. רבי חנינא first puts the burden of proof on the creditor. רבי יוחנן's rule, which אביי supports from a משנה about a tree near a city, puts it on the orphans, because land ready to be collected counts as already collected. If the orphans do prove their claim, they are paid for the improvement in money, not land, based on שמואל's list of three cases. רבינא challenges the list's case of a creditor paying buyers. The גמרא answers that it depends on whether the debt covers the land plus the improvement, and it narrows the case to an אפותיקי. A new משנה then teaches when the שביעית year counts in a field rental and how long an employer has to pay each kind of worker. The גמרא brings the פסוקים behind the pay windows and teaches that לא תלין is broken only at the first morning, while later delay breaks בל תשהא. The amud ends with a ברייתא about hiring workers through a friend, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי חנינא assumes the land belongs to the orphans
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא first thinks the land is in the possession of the יתומים, so the בעל חוב must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא thought to say: the land is in the orphans' possession, so the creditor has to bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives his first opinion on who must prove who improved the land. He puts the burden of proof on the creditor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The orphans are the ones holding the land right now. The usual rule is that whoever wants to take something away from the person holding it must prove his claim. So רבי חנינא says the creditor must prove that the father made the improvement.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say. This is a first assumption that may be corrected.
In the presumed possession of
Orphans (here, the heirs of the debtor)
Creditor
To bring proof (to carry the burden of proof)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase סבר רבי חנינא למימר signals that this is only רבי חנינא's first thought. Do not treat it as the final הלכה, because the next step reports a different view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina thought to say:
The land stands in the possession of the orphans,
and it is upon the creditor to bring proof.
phrases.notes: The proof is about who improved the land. The orphans say they did, and the creditor says their father did.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The land is presumed to be the orphans', so the creditor must prove that the father made the improvement.

steps.title: An elder quotes רבי יוחנן: the orphans must prove
steps.stepSummary: An elder reports that רבי יוחנן said the burden of proof is on the יתומים, not on the creditor.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said to them: this is what רבי יוחנן said. The orphans have to bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: An elder disagrees with רבי חנינא's assumption by quoting רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן put the burden of proof on the other side, on the orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reverses step 1. רבי חנינא said the creditor must prove his claim, and now רבי יוחנן's tradition says the orphans must prove theirs. The reason is given in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain elder (an unnamed old scholar)
Thus said (introduces a quoted tradition)

phrases.english: A certain elder said to them,
Thus said Rabbi Yochanan:
It is upon the orphans to bring proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ הַהוּא סָבָא, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns רבי חנינא's assumption by quoting רבי יוחנן
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי חנינא's placement of the burden of proof on the creditor
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי חנינא treated the land as fully in the orphans' possession. The reason for rejecting this is explained in the next step.

steps.title: Why the orphans must prove: land ready to be collected counts as collected
steps.stepSummary: Land that is ready to be collected is treated as if the creditor already has it, so the יתומים must prove their claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Since the land is ready to be collected, it is treated as if it were already collected, so the orphans have to bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יוחנן's ruling and gives it. The land is so close to being collected that we treat it as already in the creditor's hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The orphans are physically holding the land, but legally the land is already set aside for the creditor. So in this case the creditor counts as the one holding it. That makes the orphans the ones trying to take something away, and they must prove their claim.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
It stands ready for collection
It is like something already collected

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's principle: something that is ready to be collected is treated as already collected. This flips who counts as the holder, and so it flips who must bring proof.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
The land, since it stands ready for collection,
is like something already collected,
and it is upon the orphans to bring proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the orphans must bring proof even though they hold the land
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Land ready for collection counts as already collected, so the creditor is treated as the holder.

steps.title: אביי cites a משנה about a tree near a city
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a משנה: when it is uncertain whether a tree or a city came first, the owner cuts down the tree and gets no payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: we have also learned this in a משנה. If it is uncertain whether this came first or that came first, he cuts it down and is not paid.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings support for רבי יוחנן's principle from a משנה. This step only quotes the source; the next step explains how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, a tree that is too close to a city must be cut down no matter what. Whether the owner gets paid depends on which came first. When nobody knows which came first, he gets nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this (a supporting source)
Uncertainty, doubt
He cuts down (the tree)
Money, payment

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Abaye said: We too have also learned this:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בבא בתרא (24b) about a tree growing too close to a city.

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק זֶה קָדַם וְסָפֵק זֶה קָדַם –
phrases.english: If it is uncertain whether this came first or that came first,
phrases.notes: "This" and "that" are the tree and the city.

phrases.english: he cuts it down and does not give money.
phrases.notes: The tree's owner cuts it down, and the city does not pay him for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support רבי יוחנן's principle
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that something ready to be collected counts as already collected
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בבא בתרא about a tree near a city whose timing is uncertain

steps.title: Applying the tree case to the loan document
steps.stepSummary: Since the tree must be cut anyway, its owner must prove he deserves payment. In the same way, the loan document is ready to be collected, so the יתומים must prove their claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see: since the tree is going to be cut down anyway, we tell its owner, "Bring proof and then take payment." So too, this document is ready to be collected, so it counts as already collected, and the orphans must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains how the משנה proves רבי יוחנן's point, then applies it to the creditor and the orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tree owner still has his tree, yet he must prove he deserves payment, because the tree is already set to be cut down. In the same way, the orphans still hold the land, but the creditor's document has already set it aside for collection. So the burden of proof falls on the orphans.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently, so we see (draws an inference)
It stands to be cut down
Bring proof and take
Document (here, the loan document)

steps.whatToRemember: The tree case and the land case work the same way. Whatever is already set to be cut or collected is treated as if it has happened, so the side holding it must bring proof.

phrases.english: Apparently, since it stands to be cut down,
we say to him: Bring proof and take.
So too, this document,
since it stands ready for collection,
is like something already collected,
and it is upon the orphans to bring proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה and applies it to the loan document
steps.raayaSupportSource: The tree must be cut down anyway, so its owner must prove he deserves payment

steps.title: If the orphans prove it, רבי חנינא thinks they are paid with land
steps.stepSummary: Once the יתומים prove they made the improvement, רבי חנינא first thinks they are paid off with a portion of the land itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The orphans brought proof that they made the improvement. רבי חנינא thought to say: when we pay them off, we pay them with land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case, where the orphans do prove they improved the land. רבי חנינא gives a first opinion on how they are paid, which sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the improvement is the orphans' own, they deserve their share of its value. The new question is the form of payment. רבי חנינא's first thought is that they get part of the land, not money. The wording סבר למימר signals this is only a first thought.

keyTerms.meaning: They improved (made the land worth more)
We remove or pay off (settle with them)
Land

phrases.english: The orphans brought proof
that they improved [the land],
Rabbi Chanina thought to say:
When we pay them off,
we pay them off with land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְיתוֹ יַתְמֵי רְאָיָה דְּאִינְהוּ אַשְׁבַּחוּ, סָבַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who must prove to how the orphans are paid once they do prove it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא's first thought: orphans who prove they made the improvement are paid with a portion of the land.

steps.title: The orphans are paid in money, not land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea from step 6 that the יתומים get a portion of the land. They are paid off with money, as we learn from רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not right. We pay them off with money, as we learn from רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first idea that the יתומים are paid with part of the land. It says they get money, and it is about to bring רב נחמן's statement as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, the thought was that the יתומים are paid with a piece of the land itself. Now the גמרא says that is wrong: the creditor keeps all the land and pays them the value of the improvement in cash. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so: rejects an earlier idea
With money
We pay them off, we settle with them

phrases.english: But that is not so;
we pay them off with money,
as we learn from Rav Nachman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי חנינא's first idea that payment is made with land.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the יתומים are paid with a portion of the land
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב נחמן's rule shows that improvements are paid in money

steps.title: Three cases where improvements are paid in money
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: in three cases the court estimates the improvement and pays it in money. These are a בכור to a regular brother, a creditor or כתובה to יתומים, and a creditor to buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: In three cases the court estimates the improvement and they are paid in money: a firstborn to a regular brother, a creditor or a wife's כתובה to orphans, and a creditor to buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for step 7: שמואל's list of three cases where the improvement is paid in money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second case on the list is our exact case: a creditor taking land from יתומים. Since שמואל says the improvement there is paid in money, the יתומים get cash, not land.

keyTerms.meaning: The court estimates the value
Improvement, the added value to land
They pay them off with money
Firstborn son, who inherits a double portion
An ordinary, non-firstborn son
Buyers of land

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule the rest of the section argues about, especially its third case, a creditor paying buyers.

phrases.english: For Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel:
In three cases the court estimates the improvement for them,
and they pay them off with money,
and these are they:
a firstborn to an ordinary son,
phrases.notes: The brothers improved the field together, so the firstborn pays his brother for the improvement that ends up in the firstborn's extra share.

phrases.english: and a creditor and a wife's כתובה to orphans,
and a creditor to buyers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 7's claim.
steps.raayaObject: The יתומים are paid for improvements in money
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל's list of three cases

steps.title: רבינא asks: doesn't שמואל say the creditor takes the improvement too?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי: how can שמואל say a creditor pays buyers for the improvement, when שמואל also said a creditor collects the improvement too?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Does שמואל really hold that a creditor pays buyers? What improvement does a buyer get? Didn't שמואל say a creditor collects the improvement!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא points out that the third case on שמואל's list seems to go against another ruling of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list says a creditor pays the buyer for his improvement. But שמואל elsewhere says the creditor takes the improvement along with the land. These two rulings seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? Brings up a surprising conclusion
But didn't he say...! Points to a contradicting statement
Collects a debt

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Is this to say that Shmuel holds
that a creditor pays buyers for the improvement?
And what improvement does a buyer have coming to him?
But didn't Shmuel say:
a creditor collects the improvement!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: לְמֵימְרָא דְּסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the third case in שמואל's list from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a creditor pays buyers for improvements
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל elsewhere rules the creditor collects the improvement, which contradicts paying the buyer for it

steps.title: רבינא rules out an answer based on the size of the improvement
steps.stepSummary: רבינא suggests a possible answer: one ruling is about a big improvement and the other about a small one. He rejects it, because שמואל collected even big improvements in daily cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is not difficult, because one ruling is about an improvement that reaches the shoulders and the other is about one that does not, that cannot be. There are cases every day where שמואל let the creditor collect even an improvement that reaches the shoulders!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא is still speaking. He blocks an answer someone might give, so his question stays strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested answer splits the two rulings by how big the improvement is. But שמואל's actual rulings in court show the creditor took even big improvements. So size cannot explain the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: brings up a possible answer
Reaches the shoulders: a large improvement
Cases that happen every day

steps.confusionAlert: The answer about "shoulders" is not the גמרא's answer. רבינא brings it up only to reject it.

phrases.english: And if you will say: it is not difficult:
here it is about an improvement that reaches the shoulders,
phrases.notes: A picture phrase for a big improvement, big enough that porters could carry it away on their shoulders.

phrases.english: there it is about an improvement that does not reach the shoulders.
But there are cases every day,
where Shmuel has the creditor collect
even an improvement that reaches the shoulders!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רבינא's question by rejecting a likely answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested split based on the size of the improvement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's real rulings collected even big improvements for the creditor

steps.title: It depends on how much the debt is
steps.stepSummary: If the debt is as big as the land plus the improvement, the creditor takes everything. If the debt is smaller, the creditor pays the buyer for the improvement.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. One ruling is where he was owed as much as the land and the improvement together. The other is where he was not owed as much as the land and the improvement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא by showing that שמואל's two rulings are about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The split is not about the size of the improvement but about the size of the debt. If the debt covers land and improvement, the creditor collects both. If it covers less, he takes the land but must pay the buyer for the extra improvement.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: the two sources discuss different cases
He is owed by him
The amount, the measure

steps.whatToRemember: A creditor collects the improvement only up to the amount of his debt. If the land plus improvement is worth more than the debt, he pays the buyer for the improvement in money.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where he was owed
as much as the land and the improvement,
that is where he was not owed
as much as the land and the improvement.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּמַסֵּיק בֵּיהּ כְּשִׁיעוּר אַרְעָא וּשְׁבָחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question from steps 9-10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases by how much the debt is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's two rulings contradict each other about collecting the improvement
steps.terutzMaskana: Creditor collects the improvement only when the debt covers land plus improvement; otherwise he pays the buyer

steps.title: Why can't the buyer keep land worth his improvement?
steps.stepSummary: Some hold that a לוקח with cash can pay off a בעל חוב and keep the land. Under that view, the לוקח should be able to say: 'I can't pay you off for the whole field, but give me a piece of land equal to my שבח.'
steps.simpleTranslation: In step 11 we said that when the debt is smaller than the land plus the improvement, the creditor pays the buyer money and sends him away. That fits the view that a buyer cannot push away a creditor with cash. But some hold that a buyer with cash CAN push the creditor away. Under that view, the buyer should be able to say: 'If I had cash, I would pay you and keep the whole field. Since I don't, at least give me a piece of my land the size of my improvement!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 11, which said the creditor pays the buyer money for his improvement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the בעל חוב can send the לוקח away with money. But if a לוקח is allowed to pay off a בעל חוב with cash and keep the land, then the land is not simply the creditor's to take. So the לוקח should be able to ask for a piece of the land worth his שבח, instead of just getting money.

keyTerms.meaning: removes or pays off; sends someone away from the property
this works well according to the one who says
the improvement (the extra value the buyer added to the land)
a plot of land

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the sides. The לוקח is the one who bought the field and improved it. The בעל חוב is the creditor who comes to take the field for the seller's old debt.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לָא מַסֵּיק שִׁיעוּר אַרְעָא וּשְׁבָחָא,
phrases.english: And when he is not owed as much as the land plus the improvement,
phrases.notes: This is quoting the answer from step 11.

phrases.aramaic: דְּיָהֵיב לֵיהּ זוּזֵי לְלוֹקֵחַ וּמְסַלֵּק לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: we said he gives the buyer money and sends him away.
This works well according to the one who says:
even if the buyer has money,

phrases.aramaic: לָא מָצֵי מְסַלֵּק לֵיהּ לְבַעַל חוֹב – שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: he cannot pay off the creditor and send him away. Then it is fine.
But according to the one who says:
if the buyer has money,
he can pay off the creditor and send him away,
then let the buyer say to him:
'If I had money,
I would send you away from the whole field.'
'Now that I don't have money,
give me a plot of land
within my field, worth the amount of my improvement!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 11, using a known argument about whether a buyer can pay off a creditor with cash.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 11's rule that when the debt is smaller than the land plus the improvement, the creditor pays the buyer money for the improvement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some hold a לוקח with cash can keep the land. Under that view, a לוקח without cash should at least be able to keep a piece of land equal to his שבח, instead of being forced to take money.

steps.title: The field was set aside as the only source of payment
steps.stepSummary: The case is an אפותיקי. The debtor told the creditor, 'You can collect only from this field,' so the creditor may take the whole field and pay the buyer money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are talking about a case where the debtor made this field an אפותיקי for the creditor. He told him: 'You will be paid only from this field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 12 by narrowing the case to a field set aside as an אפותיקי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the לוקח might be able to keep a piece of land. But when the field is an אפותיקי, this field is the only place the בעל חוב can collect from. So the בעל חוב is entitled to the field itself, and the לוקח gets paid for his שבח in money.

keyTerms.meaning: here, what case are we dealing with? (the גמרא narrows the case)
a field set aside as the specific source for paying a debt
payment, repayment of a debt

steps.whatToRemember: When a field is an אפותיקי, the creditor can take the whole field and pay the buyer money for his improvement. The buyer cannot insist on keeping a piece of the land.

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
A case where the debtor set the field aside for him as an אפותיקי,
phrases.notes: An אפותיקי is a field picked out ahead of time as the place the debt gets paid from.

phrases.english: meaning he said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהֵא לְךָ פֵּרָעוֹן אֶלָּא מִזּוֹ.
phrases.english: 'You will get payment only from this field.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a field set aside as an אפותיקי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought this was any ordinary field the debtor sold, where the buyer could ask for a piece of land worth his improvement.
steps.terutzMaskana: The field was an אפותיקי, the only place the creditor can collect from. So the creditor takes the field and pays the buyer money for the improvement.

steps.title: Renting a field: does the שביעית year count?
steps.stepSummary: If someone rents a field 'for one שבוע' for 700 זוז, the שביעית year counts as part of the time. If he rents it 'for seven years,' the שביעית year does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone rents a field from his friend for one seven-year cycle for 700 זוז, the seventh year counts as one of the years. If he rented it for seven years for 700 זוז, the seventh year does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: renting a field for a stretch of time that includes the שביעית year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on the wording of the deal. 'One שבוע' means the known seven-year cycle, which already includes the שביעית year, so that year counts. 'Seven years' means seven years of using the field, so the שביעית year is not counted toward them.

keyTerms.meaning: short for מַתְנִיתִין: the משנה
one who rents a field to farm it
here: a seven-year cycle ending with שְׁבִיעִית
the seventh year, when the land is not farmed
part of the count

steps.confusionAlert: Here שָׁבוּעַ does not mean a week. It means a seven-year cycle.

phrases.english: Mishnah: One who rents a field from his friend
for one seven-year cycle for seven hundred zuz:
the seventh year counts as one of the years.
If he rented it from him for seven years
for seven hundred zuz:
the seventh year does not count as one of the years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Renting 'for one שבוע': the שביעית year counts. Renting 'for seven years': the שביעית year does not count.

steps.title: How long an employer has to pay a worker
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists, for each kind of worker, the stretch of time during which he collects his wages. The time depends on whether the job ended by day or by night.
steps.simpleTranslation: A day worker collects his pay all that night. A night worker collects all the next day. An hourly worker collects all night and all day. A worker hired for a week, a month, a year, or a seven-year cycle: if he finished during the day, he collects all that day; if he finished at night, he collects all that night and the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The same משנה moves to a second topic: the time period for paying hired workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pay period follows right after the work ends. A שְׂכִיר יוֹם finishes in the day, so the following night is his collecting time. A שְׂכִיר לַיְלָה finishes at night, so the following day is his collecting time. For long-term workers, it depends on when the job actually ended. Daytime gives him the rest of that day; nighttime gives him the night and the following day.

keyTerms.meaning: a worker hired for the day
collects (his wages)
a worker hired by the hour
left, meaning finished his job

steps.whatToRemember: Pay time is set by when the work ends. Work that ends by day is paid by the end of that day or the next night (depending on the worker). Work that ends by night is paid by the end of the next day.

phrases.english: A day worker collects his pay all night.
phrases.notes: He means the employer has this whole stretch of time to pay him.

phrases.english: A night worker collects all the following day.

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכִיר שָׁעוֹת – גּוֹבֶה כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה וְכׇל הַיּוֹם.
phrases.english: An hourly worker collects all night and all day.
A worker hired for a week, a worker hired for a month,
a worker hired for a year, or a worker hired for a seven-year cycle:
if he finished during the day, he collects all that day;

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא בַּלַּיְלָה – גּוֹבֶה כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה וְכׇל הַיּוֹם.
phrases.english: if he finished at night, he collects all that night and all the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second part of the same משנה, moving to a new topic: paying workers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Day worker: all night. Night worker: all day. Hourly worker: all night and day. Long-term workers: all day if they finished by day, all night and day if they finished at night.

steps.title: A day worker can be paid all through the night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from a פסוק that a day worker's pay window is the whole night after his work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: How do we know a day worker can collect all night? The פסוק says: 'The wages of a hired worker shall not stay with you overnight until morning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining our משנה. It brings a ברייתא that finds a source for the day worker's pay window.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the wages may not stay with the employer 'until morning.' So the deadline is morning, and the employer has the whole night to pay. This fits a day worker, whose work ends when night begins.

keyTerms.meaning: A worker hired for the daytime
Collects (his wages)
Do not let it stay overnight
A hired worker's wages

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
From where do we know about a day worker
that he collects his pay all night?
phrases.notes: In other words, the employer has the whole night to pay him and still isn't late.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"The wages of a hired worker shall not stay overnight
with you until morning."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן לִשְׂכִיר יוֹם שֶׁגּוֹבֶה כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the משנה's pay windows from Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A day worker's pay window is the whole following night, until morning.

steps.title: A night worker can be paid all through the day
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא learns from a second פסוק that a night worker's pay window is the whole following day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know a night worker can collect all day? As it says: 'On his day you shall give him his wages.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the second kind of worker, the one who works at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק says 'on his day,' so the deadline is the end of the day. That fits a night worker, whose work ends at daybreak. Together, the two פסוקים give the two pay windows.

keyTerms.meaning: A worker hired for the night
On his day (during that same day)

phrases.english: And from where do we know about a night worker
that he collects his pay all day?
As it says: "On his day you shall give him his wages."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן לִשְׂכִיר לַיְלָה שֶׁגּוֹבֶה כׇּל הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the pair: the day worker came first, now the night worker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A night worker's pay window is the whole following day.

steps.title: Why not match the verses the other way around?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't apply the 'until morning' פסוק to the night worker and the 'on his day' פסוק to the day worker.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it the other way around!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the way the ברייתא matched each פסוק to a worker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים themselves don't say which worker each one is about. Someone could argue that 'on his day' fits the worker who works by day. Then he would be paid during the day, and the night worker during the night.

keyTerms.meaning: But say the opposite!

phrases.english: But say the opposite!
phrases.notes: He means: link 'until morning' to the night worker and 'on his day' to the day worker.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how Steps 16–17 matched the פסוקים to the workers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's matching of each פסוק to a type of worker.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים don't say which worker they mean, so the opposite matching seems just as possible.

steps.title: Wages are only owed once the job is finished
steps.stepSummary: Pay becomes due at the end of the work, so the pay window must be the time period right after the job ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hiring is only paid at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a basic rule: wages are owed only when the work is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A day worker finishes at nightfall, so his window has to be the night. A night worker finishes at daybreak, so his window has to be the day. The opposite matching would demand payment before the work is even finished, which makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Hiring (the payment owed for a hire)
Is paid / becomes due
At the end

steps.whatToRemember: The pay window always starts when the job ends: a day worker has the following night, and a night worker has the following day.

phrases.english: Hiring is not paid
except at the end.
phrases.notes: The end of the work period, when the job is finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical principle that settles which פסוק belongs to which worker
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either פסוק could fit either worker.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pay is only owed after the work ends, so each worker's window must come after his shift.

steps.title: 'Until morning' means the לאו is broken only once
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא asks why the extra words 'until morning' are needed. It answers that they teach that the employer breaks this לאו only at the first morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Once it says 'do not let the wages stay overnight with you,' don't I already know that means until morning? Why does it add 'until morning'? To teach that he breaks the איסור only at the first morning.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא finds a lesson in words of the פסוק that seem extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Do not let it stay overnight' already means 'don't hold it past the morning.' So the words 'until morning' seem extra. They teach that the לאו of לא תלין is broken one time only, at the first morning, and is not broken again every morning after that.

keyTerms.meaning: From what is implied
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
Breaks (an איסור)
The first morning

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean late payment becomes allowed after the first morning. It only means this one לאו is not broken again. The next steps show that a different איסור still applies.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: From what is implied by what it says,
"The wages of a hired worker shall not stay overnight with you,"
don't I know that it means "until morning"?
Why does the verse say "until morning"?
It teaches that he does not break the איסור
except up to the first morning alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּשְׁמַע שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לֹא תָלִין פְּעֻלַּת שָׂכִיר אִתְּךָ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁעַד בֹּקֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the 'לא תלין' פסוק from Step 16 to learn something new from its extra words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לאו of לא תלין is broken only once, at the first morning.

steps.title: What if he delays even longer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is when the employer keeps holding back the pay after the first morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: From then on, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking about delays after the first morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 taught that the לאו of לא תלין is broken only once. So we need to know whether any further delay is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: From here on

phrases.english: From then on, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the limit taught in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether holding back wages after the first morning breaks any איסור.

steps.title: רב: he breaks 'בל תשהא'
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that after the first morning, the employer breaks the איסור of 'בל תשהא', do not delay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: He breaks the איסור of 'do not delay.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question: further delay is still forbidden, under a different איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The specific לאו of לא תלין is used up after the first morning. But a more general איסור, 'בל תשהא', still applies to every further delay.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not delay (the איסור against holding back what you owe)

phrases.english: Rav said:
He breaks the איסור of "Do not delay."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם בַּל תְּשַׁהֶא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After the first morning, delaying the pay breaks בל תשהא.

steps.title: רב יוסף gives the פסוק for 'בל תשהא'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף shows where רב's איסור comes from: a פסוק in משלי against putting off a neighbor when you have the means to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is the פסוק? 'Do not say to your neighbor, Go and come back, tomorrow I will give, when you have it with you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף supports רב's ruling by naming its source in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes someone who has the money but keeps telling the other person to come back tomorrow. That is exactly an employer who keeps delaying after the first morning. So the איסור of בל תשהא covers him.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק (that teaches this)?
Go and come back
When you have it with you

steps.whatToRemember: Holding back a day worker's pay past his window breaks לא תלין once, at the first morning. After that, every further delay breaks בל תשהא, learned from the פסוק in משלי.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: What is the verse?
"Do not say to your neighbor: Go and come back,
and tomorrow I will give, when you have it with you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב's ruling in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that further delay breaks בל תשהא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 3:28: 'Do not say to your neighbor, Go and come back, tomorrow I will give, when you have it with you.'

steps.title: Hiring workers through a friend: neither one breaks בל תלין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if someone tells his friend to go hire workers for him, neither of them breaks בל תלין. The owner is exempt because he did not personally hire the workers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A person tells his friend, 'Go out and hire workers for me.' Neither of them breaks the איסור of בל תלין. This one, the owner, is exempt because he did not hire them himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a case where the hiring is done through a middleman. It gives the ruling and starts listing the reason each person is exempt. The reason for the second person comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא spoke about an employer who hired workers himself. Here a friend does the hiring for the owner, and the ברייתא says neither one breaks בל תלין. The owner is exempt because the לאו applies to the person who actually hired the workers, and the friend did that, not the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Go out and hire for me.' The owner sends someone to do the hiring for him.
Workers, hired laborers
Both of them. Here this means the owner and the friend who did the hiring.
Because he did not hire them

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the workers get no pay. The ברייתא only says neither person breaks the specific לאו of בל תלין. The workers still have to be paid.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ צֵא שְׂכוֹר לִי פּוֹעֲלִים –
phrases.english: One who says to his friend: Go out and hire workers for me,
both of them do not violate the prohibition of 'do not keep wages overnight.'
phrases.notes: 'Both' means the owner who wanted the workers and the friend who went out and hired them.

phrases.english: This one, because he did not hire them,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the owner. The ברייתא gives the friend's reason right after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ צֵא שְׂכוֹר לִי פּוֹעֲלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting out when the לאו and the איסור of delay apply, the גמרא brings a ברייתא with a case where the hiring was done through a middleman.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the owner sends a friend to hire workers, neither of them breaks בל תלין. The owner is exempt because he did not hire the workers himself.
